text: With Snowpipe, Streams, and Tasks chosen, we whiteboard the actual shape the data takes inside Snowflake -- three layers, before a single object exists.
Raw is Snowpipe's dumb, append-only landing zone. Curated is kept within minutes of raw by a Stream and a scheduled Task. Gold is dbt's job, run via Airflow -- aggregation, not freshness.
The Task is gated on SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA, so it merges new rows into curated roughly every minute and costs nothing the rest of the time.
Three rules protect this design: raw never contains business logic, gold is never allowed to read raw directly, and dbt aggregates an already-fresh table instead of racing to catch it up.
Next: the Terraform plan for exactly which warehouses, roles, and schemas this flow needs to run on.
